that cello entry around the first major drop just… hollows you out. there's something about tuning down to 448Hz that makes the resonance sit in your chest differently than standard pitch — like the grief isn't performed, it's just *present*. did gibran say anywhere why he chose 448 specifically over the more common 432Hz detuning?

It’s fascinating how those specific frequencies can change the way we feel the music, thank you for noticing that detail! ❤🌌
Just to clarify though, Gibran originally wrote the piece at the natural/standard tuning, the 448Hz tuning was actually my own choice for this version. I wanted to give it that slightly deeper, more melancholic resonance and see how it would feel. 🎹🖤

According to Islam, Jesus (Isa) is one of God’s greatest prophets and messengers, born miraculously to Mary without a human father. He performed extraordinary miracles, such as healing the sick and bringing the dead back to life, but always by God’s permission, showing that his power was not divine in itself. The Qur’an clearly teaches that Jesus was not the son of God, but a servant and messenger of God, just as all prophets were. It also rejects the belief that he was killed or crucified, stating that “they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them” (Qur’an 4:157), and that God raised him to Himself (4:158). Therefore, in Islam, Jesus did not die on the cross; he remains alive by God’s will and will return before the end of time. His miraculous birth does not make him divine—just as Adam was created without either a father or mother, Jesus’ creation was simply another sign of God’s power.
